transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-04-29 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Desai (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE notes), Maya Chen (Heliostat Head of ML), Ethan Royce (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Security), Jordan Lee (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be incomplete):
- Heliostat is evaluating Dedicated capacity for low-latency inference across hosted vs private options. They need tenant isolation for multi-product lines and predictable burst handling for peak events. Security and KMS are blockers for Private path.

Topics:
- Current infra and where models run
- Bursting profile and pre-warm strategies
- Isolation: tenant fencing, VPC vs shared with fencing
- KMS/HSM and audit requirements
- Latency SLOs and cost tradeoffs
- Next steps and baseline test plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm lena, AE on the account, and ravi will run the technical bits. can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Maya (Heliostat): maya here, head of ml, i own model roadmap and endpoint SLAs.
[00:16] Ethan (Heliostat): ethan, infra lead, i care about networking, vpc, pre-warm, things that keep our latency stable.
[00:20] Priya (Heliostat): priya, security and compliance. SOC 2, kms, audit logs are on my checklist.
[00:25] Ravi (Redwood): awesome, thanks. goal for today: understand your reservation needs for dedicated gpus, how isolation must work for product lines, and the expected burst patterns so we can propose a config.

[01:05] Jordan (Heliostat): to start, high level — we have two core product lines: realtime chat features (sync, 150-400ms SLO ideally) and a batch scoring pipeline for nightly runs. realtime is our critical path, spikes during marketing events.

[02:10] Maya: our production models are 13B/70B families — some quantized — and we also plan to bring a fine-tuned variant later this quarter. current traffic: 5k qps baseline across all endpoints, but during promos it jumps to 18-20k qps for ~10-15 minutes.

[03:12] Ethan: we currently run on K8s with a mix of spot and reserved GPUs, but the preemption on spot is painful for realtime. hence interest in Redwood Dedicated for guaranteed capacity and a better prewarm story.

[03:55] Ravi: ok good — couple clarifying q's: when you say jumps to 20k qps is that per second requests or tokens? are those short prompts ~100 tokens or longer?
[04:08] Maya: mostly requests, avg prompt ~180 tokens and responses about 60 tokens, although some longer threads hit 800 tokens.

[05:00] Lena: good, and are those spikes predictable — like calendar events — or ad hoc?
[05:06] Jordan: mostly predictable, tied to product launches and email pushes, so windows are 5-20 minutes but can happen couple times a day around launches.

[06:20] Priya: security quick note — our legal requires customer data not leave region, and we need KMS integration for secrets and keys. is KMS supported in Dedicated and Private?
[06:34] Ravi: yes we support KMS integrations for Private deployment and Dedicated has options depending on host — for our Redwood Private we do customer-managed keys via supported KMS providers; for hosted/dedicated, we offer bring-your-own-key in dedicated plans, i'll follow up with specifics.

[07:15] Ethan: important: we need tenant-level isolation — we have different business units and some want strict separation. can dedicated provide physical isolation versus multi-tenant sharing?

[07:28] Ravi: we have two main patterns — dedicated reserved GPU pools that are isolated at the node level (tenant fencing, single-tenant nodes), or shared pools with strict namespace isolation and strong quotas. for strict separation we'd recommend dedicated single-tenant node pools.

[08:02] Maya: and that adds cost, correct?
[08:05] Lena: yes typically single-tenant reservation carries a premium given capacity exclusivity but gives predictable tail latency and security surface benefits.

[09:10] Ethan: about burst — can we pre-warm a hot pool to absorb spikes and then spillover to shared warm nodes? how fast can pre-warm scale up?

[09:25] Ravi: two mechanisms: warm hotpools (idle instances with KV cache primed) and on-demand burst to compatible model variants — warm pool can serve immediately with minimal cold start. warm pool sizing depends on your tail QPS. we also do fast provisioning of compatible quantized model variants which are cheaper to spin up. typical pre-warm to handling tens of percent extra load is sub-30s; heavier ramp requires more reserved capacity.

[10:40] Jordan: sub-30s sounds good but our SLO needs sub-200ms p95 for core chat — any data on p95 when spilling to warm pool?

[11:00] Ravi: in our benchmarks, warm pool p95 added ~60-120ms compared to fully warmed dedicated nodes, depends on model size and tokenization. for 13B family numbers are on lower end, 70B higher. we'll run baseline tests with your prompts to get more accurate numbers.

[12:20] Priya: when you say "compatible model variant" does that change outputs? we can't have drift for certain regulated flows.
[12:28] Ravi: good point — compatible variants can be quantized or trimmed versions; we recommend canary evals and quality regression checks tied to prompt sets. for regulated flows you can pin those routes to only run on exact variants (no fallback) to avoid drift.

[13:15] Maya: timeline question — we aim to launch in Q3. what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated?

[13:25] Lena: onboarding is typically 4-8 weeks from contract for standard Dedicated with reserved pools, less if you accept hosted with VPC peering. Private deployments for on-prem take longer (8-12+ weeks) depending on network and KMS provisioning.

[14:10] Ethan: network topology — we need VPC peering, static egress IPs for allowlists, and support for private subnets. do you support customer-managed VPC peering for Dedicated?

[14:25] Ravi: yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and private networking. we can provide static egress IPs and NAT configs. for strict on-prem we offer a Private control plane option.

[16:00] Jordan: ok cost — can you explain cost drivers? reserved nodes, warm pools, burst execution — what's the delta we should expect?

[16:18] Lena: cost drivers: reserved node hours (base), warm pool/minutes, on-demand burst hourly or per-second usage, storage for models, and data egress. warm pools are cheaper than fully reserved nodes but still incur cost. we'll send a pricing sheet that shows example scenarios for your traffic shape.

[17:30] Ethan: auditability — we need full request logs, redaction controls, retention windows 7 years for certain enterprises — is that possible?

[17:45] Ravi: we provide audit logs and configurable retention; long-term retention can be an add-on. we can also integrate with your SIEM for real-time forwarding.

[19:05] Priya: SOC 2 docs? which certifications do you have, and are there penetration test reports we can view?

[19:20] Lena: we are SOC 2 compliant and can share the attestations in the security pack. we also provide penetration test summaries and redaction guidance. we'll include that in the follow-up email.

[21:00] Maya: one more technical — KV cache warming for chat history, can it be persisted across pre-warm nodes so we don't lose context during spike spillover?

[21:18] Ravi: we persist KV cache in memory on warm pool nodes; spillover requires cache rehydration for new nodes which can add latency. we do prefix caching to reduce rehydrate cost; for strict stateful flows we recommend sticky routing to avoid rehydration.

[23:05] Jordan: sticky routing means we need session affinity at the app layer?
[23:12] Ravi: yes either session affinity or token-aware routing from the app so user sessions remain on the same warm node. we have SDK hooks to help.

[25:00] Ethan: we'd like to see a failure mode: what happens when both reserved and warm pool saturate?

[25:12] Ravi: fallback policies: (1) fallback to a compatible lower-cost variant (with canary flags), (2) queueing with a controlled timeout and error rate, or (3) graceful degradation of non-critical endpoints. policy is configurable per-route.

[27:40] Maya: for regulated product flows, we want no fallback — fail closed to preserve correctness. can we enforce per-route hard fail?

[27:50] Lena: yes per-route policies can be hard set to fail closed. we'll document how that looks in rollout configs.

[29:00] Priya: encryption at rest and in transit — do you support customer HSM or BYOK for model keys?

[29:10] Ravi: we support BYOK via KMS integrations and in some Private configs HSM options. i'll include supported KMS vendors in the security pack.

[31:00] Jordan: curious about autoscaling — is there predictive scaling so we can scale slightly ahead of spikes?

[31:12] Ravi: we have workload-aware autoscaling that can use schedule-based or predictive signals. we also offer policies to keep a minimum hot pool during business hours for predictable behavior.

[33:20] Maya: support and runbooks — we'll need playbooks for on-call, runbooks for pre-warm, and confusion around evictions. do you offer ops runbook templates?

[33:32] Lena: yes, we provide runbook templates, and for Dedicated customers we provide an onboarding SRE hour bundle to work through playbooks.

[35:10] Ethan: single-tenant nodes — what is tenancy granularly? GPU by GPU or node by node?

[35:20] Ravi: node by node — you can reserve pools where nodes are only assigned to your account. GPU isolation at PCI-e level isn't exposed; we do node-level tenancy.

[36:30] Priya: data residency — if we need EU-only, can Dedicated be deployed in EU region only?

[36:40] Lena: yes we can provision Dedicated capacity in specific regions. Private on-prem also supports EU-only zones. we'll note regional availability in the doc.

[38:05] Jordan: which metrics will show billing for bursts vs reserved? we want transparency in chargeback to product teams.

[38:18] Ravi: console exposes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route and per-model metrics. bursts are labeled as 'on-demand' in billing and we can tag usage to product teams.

[40:00] Maya: question about model versions and rollouts — can we pin routes to versions and do canary rollouts across nodes?

[40:14] Ravi: yes model pinning and canary A/B rollouts are supported; you can also set auto-fallback if a canary degrades quality beyond thresholds.

[42:00] Jordan: what about SLA? can we get latency SLO commitments for dedicated pools?

[42:12] Lena: Dedicated customers get uptime SLA; latency SLOs are part of higher-tier SLAs and we can contract p95 targets for reserved pools — will need to size appropriately.

[44:00] Priya: legal/process — we'll likely need a security review, DPAs, and a procurement loop. timeline for procurement?

[44:12] Lena: procurement typically 2-6 weeks depending on enterprise terms. security review we'll supply pack ASAP.

[46:30] Maya: ok, final quick: whats the expected delta in cost between reserved nodes and a mixed approach (reserved + warm pool + burst)? ballpark?

[46:42] Lena: ballpark depends on utilization. if you can get baseline utilization above ~60% reserved nodes are efficient. mixed approach reduces base cost but increases on-demand spend during spikes — we'll run scenarios with your traffic numbers.

[48:00] Ravi: action items recap — we'll run a small perf baseline using your 3 prompt sets, measure p95/p99 across reserved vs warm pool spill, and share numbers. Lena will send pricing and security docs.

[49:00] Maya: sounds good — priya will join the technical deep dive.

[50:00] Lena: great, i'll schedule week of May 5 for the deep dive.

[50:12] Jordan: any blockers to start a pilot?

[50:20] Lena: contract and select reserved sizing — once agreed we can start staging in 2-4 weeks.

[51:30] Priya: one last nit — can you provide SOC test dates and pen test frequency?

[51:40] Lena: yes will include that in the security pack, penetration testing frequency and how to request redaction.

[53:00] Ethan: perfect. thanks everyone.

[53:10] Tom (Redwood): note: we'll attach baseline template to follow-up.

[53:55] Lena: thanks all, i'll follow up with the pricing + security docs and capture the perf baseline template.

[57:45] Maya: thanks — bye.

End of transcript.
